title: Daily resilience contract slice
summary: Project iteration record for the current daily publishing resilience refactor slice. This slice restores the safe degraded daily_tracking source-unavailable write contract, adds executable policy validation, enforces runner retries, makes Pages verification an explicit post-publish stage, adds deterministic discovery and draft-input degradation for source outages, and separates infrastructure publish exhaustion from content or safety blockers.

validation_commands: node --test tests/unit.test.js --test-name-pattern "report:write accepts source-unavailable daily tracking as degraded"
node --test tests/unit.test.js --test-name-pattern "daily runner degraded discovery artifact remains consumable by report draft and write"

node --test tests/unit.test.js --test-name-pattern "report:draft degrades missing known discovery input when explicitly allowed|report:draft does not degrade unknown missing inputs|report:draft does not degrade malformed known discovery input|daily runner wires platform exempt discovery outputs into report draft"
node --test tests/unit.test.js --test-name-pattern "daily runner writes infrastructure-exhausted correction rollup when publish and fallback fail"
node --test tests/unit.test.js --test-name-pattern "retrospective writer preserves degraded daily terminal statuses"

lessons.lesson: Recoverability policy must be explicit before broad runner behavior changes.
lessons.evidence: The resilience table now lists current daily runner stages and their retry, fallback, degrade, block, summary, and replay-fixture intent before changing the executor.
lessons.recommended_action: Use `config/daily-resilience-policy.json` as the design source for later source circuit breakers, browser fallbacks, AI repair fail-open behavior, and historical replay tests.

lessons.lesson: A degraded publish is only acceptable when the public artifact remains honest and readable.
lessons.evidence: The policy keeps page rendering, internal leakage, fake tracking components, unsafe content, and unrecoverable schema failures as blocking while allowing source-unavailable daily tracking to publish as degraded.
lessons.recommended_action: Do not widen degraded status to hide PromptLayer layout regressions, broad official snapshots, internal/debug text, or fake components.

lessons.lesson: Runner-written degraded source artifacts must be proven through the real report pipeline, not only by runner summary assertions.
lessons.evidence: A regression now feeds a runner-written builder fallback artifact into `generateReportDraft` and `writeReportDraft`, producing `quality_status.status:"degraded"`, `builder_sources_blocked`, and no blocking issues.
lessons.recommended_action: Use real-chain tests whenever adding a new degraded artifact shape or source-lane fallback.

lessons.lesson: Infrastructure exhaustion needs a distinct terminal state so operators know the report may be valid but delivery failed.
lessons.evidence: When `publish_real` and `publish_github_api_fallback` both fail, the runner now emits `infrastructure_blocked_after_fallback_exhausted`, `recover_infrastructure_publish`, and a correction retrospective with the same status.
lessons.recommended_action: Keep content/safety blockers and delivery infrastructure blockers separate in summaries, retrospectives, and recovery prompts.

lessons.lesson: Draft fallback must be narrow: degrade missing known source inputs, not arbitrary missing files or empty runs.
lessons.evidence: `report:draft --allow-degraded-inputs` now converts missing known discovery outputs into blocked public source-audit lanes, while tests prove unknown missing inputs still throw `ENOENT` and malformed known inputs still throw `SyntaxError`.
lessons.recommended_action: Keep draft recovery input-name allowlisted and rely on report-write/page/validate gates for publishability.

suggestions.issue: The daily runner had no single executable table proving which failures should retry, fallback, degrade, or block.
suggestions.evidence: `npm run resilience:validate` checks `config/daily-resilience-policy.json`, current runner stage coverage, package validation wiring, workflow contract markers, and public workflow docs.
suggestions.suggestion: Keep retry/fallback/degrade/block rules in a policy-as-code file and fail validation when runner stages or workflow docs drift from it.
suggestions.expected_benefit: Future robustness work can change runner behavior against a durable contract instead of rebuilding expectations from failed automation logs.
suggestions.promotion_path: Implemented as a committed policy file, validator, package script, workflow contract marker, feedback ledger entries, and unit tests.
validation_evidence: daily resilience policy validates current runner stages and workflow gates
report:write accepts source-unavailable daily tracking as degraded

suggestions.issue: Source-lane outages were historically treated as all-or-nothing blockers even when the public report could honestly mark a section degraded.
suggestions.evidence: Runner discovery fallback writes deterministic degraded artifacts, and the real report-chain regression proves those artifacts produce schema-aware degraded public output.
suggestions.suggestion: Allow policy-approved source outages to continue generation through explicit degraded artifacts, while preserving block reasons for unsafe or fake public content.
suggestions.expected_benefit: A partial source outage no longer prevents a publishable daily report when the degraded section is public, explicit, and schema-valid.
suggestions.promotion_path: Implemented with runner fallback artifacts, `report:write` quality status output, real-chain tests, and safety-block regression coverage.
validation_evidence: daily runner writes degraded discovery artifact after exhausted source failure
daily runner degraded discovery artifact remains consumable by report draft and write
daily runner blocks safety failures before degraded discovery fallback

suggestions.issue: Publish infrastructure exhaustion was collapsed into generic `blocked`, which hid the recovery path after both publish transports failed.
suggestions.evidence: The runner now reports `infrastructure_blocked_after_fallback_exhausted`, emits `recover_infrastructure_publish`, and retrospective schema validation preserves the status.
suggestions.suggestion: Classify terminal states by operator action: content repair, source degradation, Pages pending verification, or infrastructure publish recovery.
suggestions.expected_benefit: Automation summaries and retrospectives can trigger the right recovery action instead of sending every failed run into generic manual inspection.
suggestions.promotion_path: Implemented with terminal status handling, retrospective schema extension, and correction rollup regression tests.
validation_evidence: daily runner writes infrastructure-exhausted correction rollup when publish and fallback fail
daily runner records stdout and stderr from failed publish stages
retrospective writer preserves degraded daily terminal statuses

suggestions.issue: `report_draft` was marked degradable in policy but missing discovery input files still caused immediate `ENOENT` failures.
suggestions.evidence: Runner now passes `--allow-degraded-inputs`, and `generateReportDraft` only degrades known discovery output filenames while preserving hard failures for unknown inputs or zero readable inputs.
suggestions.suggestion: Use explicit degraded source-audit lanes for known missing discovery files instead of inventing report content or relaxing downstream validation.
suggestions.expected_benefit: Transient file/write gaps in one discovery lane no longer block generation when other discovery data is present and public degradation is honest.
suggestions.promotion_path: Implemented with CLI flag, runner wiring, policy narrowing, and positive/negative draft input tests.
